column2: ,The original formats the property with an unbounded sprintf into the shared buffer s, so the whole number reaches the menu. The reconstruction formats into a local char[8] with snprintf, which keeps 7 characters. Any value printed with 8 or more characters (for example 10000000, or a negative value with 7 digits) is cut off in the menu text. The size of the original's global s is not confirmed here, so the cap is only proven for the reconstruction. Medium: a visible UI difference for large property values, not a logic error."

,The original takes a reference (++refcount) and, on the removal path, releases it with a final drop after removeTexture (the pointer is passed by reference to removeTexture, which may clear it). The reconstruction takes the same extra reference and never releases it on this path: the only explicit drop is in the null-manager else branch. If removeTexture does not release the handle, the texture keeps one extra count and is leaked. Low: depends on removeTexture's ownership semantics, which were not checked here."

,When no goId-13 object matches the level's entry point, the original does not return null: v6 stays 0, the loop ends and returns the stale 'result' left by the last iteration, i.e. the last visited goId-13 object (an enabled or disabled spawn that does not match the entry point). The reconstruction returns nullptr in that case. Both call sites (PlayerManager-025dba-2.cpp:527 and Level-7c7f5d-3.cpp:621) fall back to the local player's position on null, so the restart position differs whenever a non-matching spawn exists. The iteration order also differs (list in the original, m_objectMap in the reconstruction), so which stale object is returned cannot be matched exactly. Not verified against a runtime trace."
